panels.rationale: Single H&E histology panel of a human vastus lateralis biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate with abundant eosinophils, matching the captioned eosinophilic polymyositis case. Eosinophilic predominance is a recognized less common/variant form of polymyositis. [raw subtype: eosinophilic polymyositis]

panels.figure_caption: Biopsy of left vastus lateralis showing an abundance of eosinophils.
in_text_mentions: and U2 SN RNP, was negative. Electromyography demonstrated myopathic motor unit potentials, fibrillation potentials, and positive sharp waves, consistent with an “irritable” myopathy. Core muscle biopsy of the vastus lateralis (Figure 1) demonstrated several foci of perimysial and endomysial infiltrate consisting primarily of lymphocytes and eosinophils. During his initial hospitalization, he had spontaneous normalization of his muscle strength and CK over five days. He was discharged without immunosuppressive therapy and was seen in follow-up two months later and continued to be in remission.
